liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Jam has a Mind Left Body feel, but reviewer hears an early version of the Dark Star jam on Dick's Picks Volume 2; Jam out of it has a Mind Left Body riff, with Jerry playing thunderous power chords [12][15]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Reviewer singles it out as a musical highlight, alongside Hard to Handle [10]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer says this Playin' starts getting jammy, stretching out more than expected [5]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Described as one of the hotter versions in circulation [7]
- **The Promised Land** (1 other source): Notes a Mary Had a Little Lamb tease inside Promised Land [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Happy Birthday David Crosby**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd71-08-14.sbd.ladner.21268.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 136 min; rated 4.5/5 by 38 [1]. Said about its sound: Each first-set song is preceded by a three-second pause; second set opens with a fade into Truckin'; Reviewer feels this recording captures the Grateful Dead's sound better than any other show they have heard [9][13]
- **gd1971-08-14.sbd.130871.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 133 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1971-08-14.sbd.trip.1451.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 136 min; rated 4/5 by 8 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; acoustics and comfortable assigned seating made the night feel different from other Bay Area shows [13]
- Features a deep introduction from Bill Graham and a birthday salute to Crosby [14]
- Phil Lesh is very high in the mix of this recording [19]
- Opening run of Bertha, Uncle, Mr. Charlie and Sugaree sounds to this listener like a Europe 72 show [5]
- Reviewer already owned the 15th and now prefers this night, calling it a favorite of the two [5]
- Reviewer sees these Berkeley shows as equal in caliber to the Hollywood 8-5/6 shows, known only from audience tapes [6]
- Reviewer prefers the 15th over this show, and notes Berkeley Community Theater recordings have a distinctive sound [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-08-14.sbd.ladner.21268.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by M. Woyczynski; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Original SHN files were nonseekable and misnamed; uploader renamed them, cleaned a splice in d1t06, and applied a shntool fix [1]
- **gd1971-08-14.sbd.130871.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording Info: SBD > MR > C > DAT; Transfer Info: DAT > Sony D8 > WAV > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > FLAC; Transferred, tracked and mastered by Bill Guarneri,… [2]
- **gd1971-08-14.sbd.trip.1451.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Trip Bates; source: SBD MR->DAT->CD [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-08-14 GD NRPS Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-08-14-gd-nrps-poster/) [22]
